_readme: Client registry for the embeddable widgets. One entry per customer.
This file is PUBLIC — it is served from widgets.906dashboard.com and read by
the widget in the visitor's browser. Put nothing in it you would not publish.
The client id is not a secret and is not access control: embedding is gated by
the frame-ancestors header in vercel.json, which is the file to edit when
adding a customer. An id copied onto an unlisted domain renders a blank frame.
Fields:
name     display name, used in the attribution link's UTM tag only
region   'up' — the only region with a widget today
spot     pin the widget to one town, or null for the regional roll-up.
Valid: mqt cph wfp mun irw grm pcm (see tools/widget-api/worker.js)
spotLabel  optional: name the viewing spot THIS client recommends, when it
differs from the default in tools/widget-api/worker.js. Applied
in the browser, so it never touches the cached data.
size     default form factor: 'card' | 'strip' | 'panel'
attribution  true keeps the 'Live data from 906 Dashboard' link.
false is the white-label tier — only sell it deliberately,
the link is the backlink and the referral traffic.
brand    presentation only. Never reaches the data request, so every
client on the same (region, spot) shares one cached payload.
The five verdict colours are NOT brandable and are not listed here: they
carry the Kp forecast, not the styling. See tools/widget-api/README.md.
light-demo exists to prove the widget works on a white site: the verdict
pill picks its own ink by luminance, so a pale brand does not wash it out.

travel-marquette.name: Travel Marquette
travel-marquette._provisional: Brand PROVISIONAL — sampled from travelmarquette.com's live CSS, not from a brand guide. Confirm before launch. Their gold #F2BB05 and rust #D74E09 are deliberately NOT used: gold is within 1.0-1.6 contrast of four of the five verdict colours, so using it as the accent would make the Kp signal unreadable as a signal. Navy ground + teal accent clears every check.
travel-marquette._spotLabel_note: Their own northern-lights page calls the M-28 Waysides in Chocolay Township "easy access points in the dark" — the right call for a visitor driving at night. It also names Sugarloaf Mountain and Wetmore Landing, and never mentions Presque Isle Park, which is what 906dashboard's aurora page picks. Without this override the widget would contradict the copy above it.
